page.layout: Top: page number and running head. Below them two circular medallion portraits, each with inscription around its edge (left: Henry III, right: Ludovica). Below the medallions one column of running text, full width, in two paragraphs.

main_text.l: HENRICVS III FR[?] ANC. ET POLON. REX[?]
LVDOVICA FRANC[?] REGINA[?]
HENRICVS III. Christianissimus Francorum, & Polono-
rum, Rex regni administrationem suscepit, post mortem fratris
Caroli noni, anno salutis 1574. Nam in Polonia certior factus
de fratris interitu, in Galliam quàm primum properat: id quod
videre licet in libris de ea re impressis. Plures Galliæ primates,
obviam ierūt, ut eius maiestatem salutarent, eíque de tam fœlici
& pernecessario Gallis adventu, summè gratularētur. Augustæ
Taurinorū exceptus fuit valde humaniter à duce Sabaudiæ
& illustrissima Margareta, ubi quasdam urbes transalpinas Duci
reddidit. Ibidem aliquid propositum de componendis Gallicis
tumultibus, sed frustrà, magno Reipublicæ damno. Interea Dux
Mompenserius princeps virtute clarus, nonnullas urbes, in re-
gione Pictonum, expugnatione capit. Rex Lugdunum venit,
magno Lugdunensium applausu & ovatione, sub finem Augu-
sti, ubi edictum constituit, quoquidem his ignoscit, qui tempo-
re fratris sui Caroli noni arma ceperūt inimica, promittitque, si
sibi obediant, securum in privatas eorum domos reditū. Fuit sa-
cratus in urbe Rhemorū, ab illustrissimo Cardinale Guisio, eius
loci Archiepiscopo, 13. Februarij. 1575. & 15. die eiusdem mensis
nobilissimam Ludovica Lotharenā clarissimi Comitis Vaude-
montij filiam, sibi matrimonio iunxit. Cúmque toto hoc anno,
omnia belli incendio flagrarent, & miserè populus à militibus
vexaretur, huic humanissimus Rex opem tulit, Pacificationis
Edicto publicato Lutetiæ 14. Maij 1576. Deum precemur ut tā-
tus Rex diutissimè Galliæ cōservetur, vivatq; annos Nestoreos.
LVDOVICA Lotharena, clarissimi Comitis Vaudemo-
ntij filia, Christianissimi Francorum & Polonorum Regis Henri-
ci tertij uxor, tantum præstat cęteris omnibus heroinis formæ
admirabili & prope divina elegātia, quantâ animi sublimitate
nobilitate, morûque & grauitate & humanitate plusquâ insigni.

page.notes: Medallion inscriptions are partly curved and hard to read; the letters at the start and end of each are doubtful and marked [?]. The printed text has u/v and long-s forms that were normalised per the rules; the medallion words "FR" and "FRANC" may be abbreviated differently. Printed accents (Cúmque) and the tilde marks (Lotharenā, elegātia, cōservetur, cōservetur) are kept as printed where clear. Some words in the second paragraph are in heavier type, which was not reproduced as bold.
